# Job Chapter 23 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 424v–425r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_023_page_001.jpg, JOB_023_page_002.jpg

---

**23:1** And-answered Iyyov and-said:

**23:2** "Also today my-complaint [sichi] [is] rebellion [meri]; my-hand [yadi] is-heavy upon my-groaning [anchati].

**23:3** Who would-give [mi yitten] I-knew [and] I-would-find-him [emtsa'ehu]; I-would-come to his-dwelling-place [tekhunato].

**23:4** I-would-set-in-order [e'erkah] [my] case [mishpat] before-him, and-my-mouth I-would-fill [with] arguments [tokhachot].

**23:5** I-would-know the-words [he would] answer-me [ya'aneni], and-I-would-understand what he-would-say to-me.

**23:6** Would-he contend [yariv] with-me in-greatness of-power [koach]? No, surely he would-give-heed [yasim] to-me.

**23:7** There [sham] an-upright-one [yashar] would-reason [nokhach] with-him, and-I-would-be-delivered [afaletah] forever from-my-judge [mi-shofeti].

**23:8** Behold, I-go forward [qedem] — and-he-is-not [there]; and-backward [achor] — and-I-cannot-perceive-him [lo avin lo].

**23:9** [To the] left [semol] when-he-works [ba'asoto] — and-I-cannot-behold [lo achazeh]; he-turns [ya'atof] [to the] right [yamin] — and-I-cannot-see [lo er'eh].

**23:10** For he-knows the-way [derekh] [that is] with-me; he-has-tested-me [bechanani] — I-shall-come-forth [etse] as-gold [ka-zahav].

**23:11** In-his-step [ba'ashuro] my-foot has-held-fast [achazah ragli]; his-way [darko] I-have-kept [shamarti] and-not turned-aside [at].

**23:12** The-commandment of-his-lips [sefatav] — and-I-have-not departed [lo amish]; from-my-portion [me-chuqi] I-have-treasured [tsafanti] the-words of-his-mouth [imrei fiv].

**23:13** But he [is] in-one [be'echad], and-who can-turn-him-back [yeshivennu]? And-his-soul [nafsho] desires [ivtah] — and-he-does [it].

**23:14** For he-will-complete [yashlim] my-decree [chuqi], and-like-these many-things [rabbot] [are] with-him.

**23:15** Therefore from-his-face [mipanav] I-am-dismayed [ebahel]; I-consider [etbonen] and-I-dread [efchad] from-him.

**23:16** And-God [El] has-made-faint [herak] my-heart [libi], and-the-Almighty [Shaddai] has-dismayed-me [hivhilani].

**23:17** For I-was-not cut-off [lo nitsmateti] before [the] darkness [mipnei choshekh], and-before-my-face [mipanai] he-covered [kissah] thick-darkness [ofel]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "my hand is heavy upon my groaning":** The Hebrew is difficult. Some read *yado* ("his hand") for *yadi* ("my hand"), yielding "his hand is heavy despite my groaning." The Leningrad Codex has *yadi*, which EMET retains.

**v.10 — "I shall come forth as gold":** The metallurgical metaphor (*bechanani* — "he has tested/assayed me") frames suffering as refining. This verse is Job's most confident statement of self-vindication in the dialogues.

**v.13 — "he is in one":** The phrase *be'echad* is ambiguous — "in one [purpose]," "as one [unified]," or "unique." The emphasis is God's sovereign unchangeability.

**v.17 — "I was not cut off before the darkness":** The final verse is notoriously obscure. Does Job fear the darkness or God? The Hebrew allows both readings.

*— EMET*
